title: Fix: termination-sequence inheritance mismatch causing customer eval regressions
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Summary: A high-severity customer escalation flagged that a suite of prompt/eval jobs (internal and customer-facing) started producing lower quality scores and truncated outputs after a serving defaults change rolled in mid-February. The root cause was a mismatch in how 'termination sequences' (the sequences used to stop generation) were inherited between SDK/client defaults and the runtime: a recent serving default that standardized sampling behavior also changed implicit termination handling in the runtime. Some clients (notably this customer's Dedicated deployment and Hosted customers using older SDKs) relied on the previous implicit inheritance behavior. This mismatch caused extra fallback tokens or missing early-stop behavior, which in turn altered end-of-generation tokens and broke deterministic eval metrics and stop-aware scoring.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use customer prompt dataset (shared via secure drive link in ticket) and their eval harness (pytest wrapper).
2) Call generation endpoint with SDK v1.8.2 and no explicit termination sequences (legacy usage).

3) Observe output contains trailing adapter tokens or fails to stop on the expected delimiter; rerun with explicit termination_sequence set to customer's previous stop value and see outputs match historical baseline.
4) Reproduce both on Hosted (api.redwood.example) and on customer Dedicated cluster (staging-dedicated-3) to confirm environment parity.
telemetry_summary: Spike in eval failures from 2026-02-20 correlating with runtime config change rollout. 87% of affected calls were from SDK versions <1.9.0 and 63% originated from dedicated clusters with custom router policies. Token-level diffs show appended "\n" or '|' tokens in 40% of failures; stop-checks in scoring harness returned false where legacy behavior returned true.
root_cause: A serving default change introduced in runtime-2.3.0 changed the priority order for termination sequence resolution: runtime now preferred model-level termination hints over SDK-requested explicit stop sequences when none were provided. Legacy clients assumed that absence of an explicit request meant 'inherit previous default stop-sequences at the API layer'. The mismatch only surfaced for customers that omit explicit termination sequences in production prompts (a common pattern in older integrations).
fix_summary: 1) Implemented explicit compatibility layer in runtime (runtime-2.3.1) that restores legacy 'inherit-if-absent' behavior unless a new compatibility flag is set. 2) Added an SDK patch (v1.9.1) that makes the default termination behavior explicit and warns users when relying on implicit inheritance. 3) Added unit+integration tests covering termination resolution permutations and end-to-end regression tests with customer's eval harness.
changesets_and_links: Customer ticket: INC-8842 (private link stored in customer CRM)
canary_and_rollout: Canary deployed runtime-2.3.1 to 5% of Hosted traffic (region us-west-2) and to a single Dedicated 'staging-like' pool for the impacted customer on 2026-03-03. Monitored token-diff heatmaps and customer eval pass rates. After 48 hours with no regression and with customer's QA sign-off, rolled to 100% Hosted on 2026-03-06 and scheduled Dedicated cluster patching during a low-traffic maintenance window on 2026-03-09.
monitoring_and_alerting: Added synthetic eval runs post-deploy (every 15 minutes) that compare outputs to baseline and emit an alert if stop-aware similarity drops >3% for 10 consecutive runs. New logs include explicit termination_resolution_reason in request traces to help debug future regressions.
customer_communication: Provided daily updates to the customer's engineering lead and CS on 2026-03-02 -> 2026-03-06. Shared mitigation steps (pin SDK to v1.9.1 or pass explicit terminationSequence) and offered Dedicated patch window. Customer reported full remediation of their eval suite after the Dedicated patch and verified metrics matched historical baselines.
postmortem_actions:
- Backfill: add an automated compatibility test matrix in CI that varies SDK version, explicit termination sequences presence/absence, and model variants.
- Docs: update SDK migration guide and runtime behavior doc to call out termination resolution ordering.
- Product: add a 'compatibility-preview' flag in Console to simulate new defaults before full rollout.
- Monitoring: keep synthetic evals for 30 days and then re-evaluate alert thresholds.
risk_and_open_items: Closed: rollout and customer verification. Open: surface top 10 customers relying on implicit termination behavior so we can proactively notify them of future default changes (PM follow-up: PM-412). Also need to validate on Private/on-prem installs where upgrade paths are manual.
